analysis.title: Positioning for Higher Rates (U.S. Equity Thematic Research, North America Equity Research compendium)
key_insights: JPM's economists expect the fed funds rate to go from 4.00% to 4.25% in December and then hold. The 10-year yield is around the ~5.00% near-term expectation, and the report cites a 5.24% 10-year in the utilities section.

Equity strategy base case is a shallow hiking cycle, a reversal of last year's insurance cuts, which equities can absorb given the earnings anchor. A broader cycle of four to five hikes would likely cause more significant downside and is not the base case.

Over the past year expectations moved from cuts to hikes. Long-dated Treasuries are down about 7% and forward P/E has compressed by about 3x, but equities are still up 12% YTD on earnings growth of 28% for 2026 and 22% for 2027.

The US 30-year yield is about 5.35%, near 20-year highs. JPM attributes the back-end selloff to central bank repricing, sticky inflation from oil and trade shocks, rising fiscal deficits, and possible crowding out as foreign investors shift toward corporate debt (LTM $403B vs ~$397B for Treasuries).

Roughly 80 years of data show an inverted U between the 10-year yield and S&P 500 multiples. With above-trend EPS growth (~15% y/y) yields can rise to ~5% before multiples de-rate. With consensus forward EPS growth above 20% and the S&P at ~18x 2027 EPS, JPM says equities could withstand a 10-year yield of ~5.5-6.0%.

Primary risk named is further geopolitical escalation in the Middle East creating a more severe inflation and growth shock. Other risks are weaker earnings growth and an abrupt, volatile bond selloff.

First-order effect on corporate interest expense should be gradual because debt is mostly fixed and long-dated. Financials' higher profitability and returns on ~$2.4T of cash offset it near term. Pressure concentrates in lower-income consumers, smaller companies, highly leveraged firms and capital-intensive industries outside the AI buildout.

Sector leadership depends on curve shape. Bear steepeners have favored Cyclicals such as Energy and Financials, bear flatteners have favored Technology, and bond proxies and long-duration sectors ex-Technology (Utilities, Real Estate, Comm Services, Staples) are most exposed. Base case keeps JPM in Growth and Quality Growth with large caps over small caps. A broader hiking cycle would argue for rotation into Low Vol.

JPM launched three thematic baskets: Beneficiaries of Higher Rates (JPRHIRTB), Beneficiaries of Lower Rates (JPRLORTB) and Agnostic Beneficiaries (JPRAGRTB). Performance lookback chart shows the baskets at 93.7, 69.7 and 97.1 rebased to 100 (labels not mapped to values in the text).

Higher-rate beneficiaries are asset-sensitive banks, BDCs, insurers, payroll and HSA float earners, net-cash restaurants and media, integrated oils, auto-parts retailers, waste services, EDA software, custom silicon and process control.

Large banks: higher rates are positive for NII through lagged deposit repricing, with a modest, manageable hit to capital from HTM and AFS marks. BAC is the more asset-sensitive pick, C benefits from non-US rates, and TFC is relatively disadvantaged by its swap book. JPM sees no 2023-style crisis risk in its universe.

BDCs: ARCC is JPM's preferred way to play higher rates, followed by BXSL. Both trade near 1.0x NAV vs 0.60-0.70x for most peers and kept their dividends. Commercial mortgage REITs (ABR, KREF) face non-accrual and resolution drag.
Insurers benefit from higher investment income. Commercial lines have net investment income of up to ~60% of earnings, reinsurers 40-60%, personal lines under 40%.
Exchanges are best positioned. CME was upgraded to Overweight on 10/22/26 on trading velocity in rate futures and spread income on ~$2bn of corporate cash and ~$150bn of customer collateral.

Semis are generally a headwind, with analog (NXPI, ON, GFS) most exposed on auto and industrial. JPM favors EDA (CDNS, SNPS), custom silicon (AVGO) and process control (KLAC) as tied to durable R&D spending.

AI infrastructure builders are the most rate-exposed in tech and communications. CoreWeave has ~8-9% cost of debt, Oracle has net cash capex of ~$70B dependent on external funding, and IREN expects $25-30B of FY27 capex. JPM says AI-linked debt spreads are widening and sentiment on AI monetization has deteriorated.

Hyperscalers face higher borrowing costs and AI ROIC scrutiny. JPM estimates 2027 capex of $378B for Alphabet, $366B for Amazon and $243B for Meta, with large projected debt issuance for all three, but cites investment-grade balance sheets and cash-generative core businesses.

Housing-linked names are hurt. Construction materials analysts now expect no meaningful residential recovery until 2028 (previously 2H27). Mortgage rates peaked near 7.4-7.5% in early October and are ~7.3% now. Fannie Mae cut its 3Q26 origination forecast to $508B from $590B in July.

Consumer backdrop is described as resilient. Chase card discretionary spend was +6.7% y/y in September, and households hold ~$8T more cash than in 2019. Risk is concentrated in leveraged or rate-dependent names such as FUN and BC.

Utilities trade at an 11.1% discount to the S&P 500 vs ~9.9% implied by a 20-year regression at current yields. FE, ES and WEC are flagged as most exposed to holdco debt refinancing and ETR as the most balanced.
Biotech has underperformed since Labor Day (NBI -3.37% vs SPX -1.23% from 9/4 to 10/23/2026). CROs are the most negatively exposed life-science group via early-stage biotech funding.
Large-cap pharma is seen with minimal rate impact, with LLY, GILD and ABBV named as top names.
Gold has been inversely correlated with real yields. JPM says gold lost about $17/oz per 1bp rise in US 10Y real yields from March to July 2026.
Security software is treated as agnostic because AI demand is outweighing rate sensitivity. Software multiples historically move inversely with rates.

charts_described: Figure 14 shows semis lagged for much of the 2022-23 hiking cycle (11 hikes) before rebounding as hikes neared an end, while in the 2015-18 cycle (9 hikes) stronger fundamentals supported sustained outperformance.
Figure 1 is described in its title as P/E sensitivity to rising yields by EPS growth regime, 1950-present, with no values given in the text.
Figure 16 compares average security software EV/NTM sales against the 10-year yield from 12/31/2025 to 10/23/2026, with the text saying AI tailwinds have been a more significant factor than rates.
vol_and_positioning: Long/short debasement trades should remain popular into economic data prints, FOMC meetings and Treasury policy actions, though JPM sees the rate rise as anchored to fundamentals (stable long-end swap spreads, marginally higher breakevens).
Rate-sensitive ETF flows are flagged as keeping marginal pricing power in gold as investors moved on from the debasement trade.
Historically bank stocks and the broader market dip early in hiking cycles, recover as earnings hold, then lag on slowdown concerns.
geopolitical: Further geopolitical escalation in the Middle East is named as the primary risk, with oil price sensitivity to equities referenced.
Strait of Hormuz: sentiment on its opening is cited as a swing factor for coatings stocks via commodity prices and rate expectations.
Ongoing oil and trade shocks cited as drivers of sticky inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings growth (28% in 2026, 22% in 2027) and a shallow hiking cycle let equities absorb yields up to ~5.5-6.0% on the 10-year, with AI-led productivity supporting multiples.
tension_points.bear_case: A broader cycle of four to five hikes, a reacceleration in inflation or an abrupt bond selloff would drive more significant downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker earnings growth, a forward curve pricing 4-5 hikes, or Middle East escalation creating a severe inflation and growth shock.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have investment-grade balance sheets and cash-generative core businesses, and returns are visible (AWS AI and chips above $25B ARR).
tension_points.bear_case: Higher borrowing costs and widening spreads on AI-linked debt raise ROIC scrutiny, with projected debt issuance of $210B to $300B per hyperscaler for 2027E-2029E.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained spread widening on AI-linked debt or failure of AI monetization to justify the spending.
